<reason>A established a concrete comparison-and-coordination harm that total-price disclosure alone cannot solve, then defended a flexible disclosure boundary and answered responsibility questions directly. B usefully distinguished existing fee compliance from new house-rule obligations, but overstated both voluntary disclosure’s reliability and the certainty of regulatory costs. Its boilerplate and litigation mechanisms remained insufficiently developed to outweigh earlier access to disqualifying conditions. A also correctly rejected B’s characterization of optional checkout repetition as mandated duplication.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s argument that earlier access and later confirmation are complements directly undermined B’s claim that checkout attention justified delaying disclosure. B legitimately refined its boilerplate argument around omission penalties, but did not establish why moving existing rules earlier would substantially worsen comprehension.</best_rebuttal>
